newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-PARREIRA SACKED BY SAO PAULO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARREIRA SACKED BY SAO PAULO.

text.p: Carlos Alberto Parreira, Brazil's 1994 World Cup winning coach, was sacked by Sao Paulo on Wednesday following a run of 10 games without a win in the Brazilian championship.
Sao Paulo directors made their decision under enormous pressure from the club's fans, who had been baying for Parreira's blood for several weeks.
At several games fans have chanted the name of Tele Santana, who was in charge of the team for five successful years until resigning due to ill-health in January.

Parreira made a brief appearance at a club training session on Wednesday but did not speak to the media. Striker Valdir said: "He came over, said goodbye and see you around and that was the only contact we had."

Earlier on Wednesday, Parreira had given an interview to the Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper in which he said: "I'm suffering a cowardly persecution...I still don't understand what crime I have committed."

Apart from poor results, which have seen Sao Paulo slip from first to 17th in the Brazilian championship, Parreira had been accused of deploying over-cautious tactics -- a criticism also levelled against him when he was in charge of Brazil.
Since the World Cup, Parreira has coached Spanish club Valencia and Turkey's Fenerbahce, who he led to the Turkish championship last year.
In addition to Brazil, Parreira coached Kuwait at the 1982 World Cup finals and United Arab Emirates in 1990.
